Excellencies, dear colleagues, could I request you to take your seats again. And let me call the meeting to order. I would now like to put some text on the screen where we stand. With regard to para 25, and I would like to do this in a formal session. Before we adopt this para later this evening, let me record the understandings on which the Group has proceeded. Para 25, and I have said it on numerous occasions, is a working characterization. The characterization is framed in terms of capability. The words "is capable of" govern the whole of what follows, including the manner of engagement. The characterization does not turn on the purpose for which a system was designed or on its primary function. The Group considered and did not adopt proposals framed in those terms. What matters is what a system is capable of doing. The chapeau of para 25 and sub-para are to be read together as a single package. Subpara 25b is based on the effects of the system. When read together, this means that any system with the mentioned capability is used, when any system with the mentioned capability is used, is included in the characterisation. Furthermore, delegations also sought clarification on the expression "specific group of targets" in the second sentence of para 25. Let me record the understanding on which the Group has proceeded. The expression refers to a grouping of targets that the personnel planning, deciding upon, or carrying out the attack have themselves determined. For example, a particular formation that the personnel identified. It's different from a set of potential targets or characteristics thereof in the first sentence of the same sub-para. A category or class of targets within which the system itself determines which objects to identify, select and engage falls within the first sentence, and accordingly does not exclude a system from this characterization. The two sentences of subparagraph are to be read together and consistently. Would any delegation like to take the floor at this stage? I recognize the distinguished representative of Turkey. You have the floor.

Thank you, Chair. Just to be clear, I am not going to talk about 25. We wish to extend our sincere appreciation and warm congratulations to you and your team for your able stewardship of our deliberations and for bringing our work over the past three years to the threshold of consensus. We're almost there. We also thank UNODA and CCW ISU for their invaluable contributions. The set of elements before us represents a significant achievement and a testament to the sustained efforts, patience and determination invested by all delegations. These elements will provide a solid basis for carrying this work forward under our future mandate to be determined by the seventh review conference. We also wish to express our appreciation to all high contracting parties for their constructive, flexible and forward-looking engagement, as well as for the spirit of compromise and accommodation that has guided our collective efforts throughout this process. I believe this spirit will help us gavel a report by consensus later tonight. Chair, we prepared this statement to deliver upon adoption of the report. However, as this will not be possible, we're grateful to be able to take this opportunity to put on record the following. Based on the paragraphs we agreed on so far, Turkey is ready to join consensus on the final report on the clear understanding that the set of elements contained in subsection A of the conclusions is without prejudice to the nature of any possible future instrument. and does not in of itself create new legal obligations or alter or expand the existing rights and obligations of states under international law. This is consistent with and reinforced by the qualifiers contained in recommendation section in paragraph 46A of the report, which are essential for us to join consensus. We further place on record our understanding that formulations expressed as must in the current text including but not limited to paragraphs 31, 32, 34, 37, 41, 42 as they stand, are intended to reflect existing obligations and apply to each state only in accordance with and to the extent of that state's own obligations under applicable international law, including in case of states such as Turkey that are not party to Additional Protocol I to the Geneva Conventions. Accordingly, the legal reviews referred to in paragraph 37 are to be conducted by each State in accordance with its own obligations. We also place on record that our acceptance of these formulations should not be understood as an acknowledgement that they reflect settled rules of customary international law applicable irrespective of a State's treaty relationships. It reflects rather our willingness to join consensus on this text as a technical reference on the basis of the understanding set out in the statement. Turkey further understands that the characterization in paragraph 25 is descriptive and without prejudice to future understandings as stated in paragraph 25C, and that paragraph 36D does not preclude autonomous functions performed within mission parameters previously authorized by a human being, including for self-protection and navigation. We also wish to put on record our understanding that references throughout the text to control and human judgment do not establish new legal standards beyond existing IHL. Also, they should not be read as requiring constant direct human control over the operation of a weapon system at every phase of its use. Let me also recall Turkey's consistent position that this group's work should neither serve as a step towards nor constitute the basis for a legally binding instrument or laws. We remain of the view that our discussions are most productively pursued within the framework of CCW on the basis of consensus and that any document should retain the character of a framework capturing areas of convergence among states. Finally, we wish to underline that nothing in this final report should be understood to affect the ability of States to pursue legitimate research, development and industrial activities, nor should it be read as requiring the sharing of proprietary technologies, source code or training data sets. We ask that this statement be reflected in the record of this meeting and made available in writing on the official website of the Convention. Thank you for your patience.

And so will be done. I thank the distinguished representative of Turkey. Any further requests to speak on this issue? Then I would like to thank the delegation of Turkey for her statement. And as we still have some work to do for the finalization of the report, I recommend that we suspend the meeting that we stop the clock and that the High Contracting Parties reconvene in Room 3 at 1930 hours, 7.30 evening, to finalise and adopt the final report. The meeting is suspended.
